posts.text:
In 290 BC, Rome was just one power in central Italy.

By 201 AD, it ruled Britain, the Sahara coast, and Mesopotamia — the whole Mediterranean as a Roman lake.

500 years of conquest, mapped year by year — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ 290 BC: Rome finally breaks the Samnites after three brutal wars and controls most of peninsular Italy.

241 BC: the First Punic War ends. Sicily becomes Rome's first overseas province — the model for every conquest that follows.

2/ 218-201 BC: Hannibal crosses the Alps and wins battle after battle, but Rome refuses to quit.

In 202 BC Scipio beats him at Zama in North Africa. By 201 BC Carthage surrenders Spain and its fleet. Rome is now the strongest state in the western Mediterranean.

3/ 146 BC is the brutal turning point: Rome destroys Carthage AND Corinth in the same year.

Africa and Greece become provinces. Two ancient rivals are erased within months of each other.

4/ 58-51 BC: Caesar conquers all of Gaul.

30 BC: Egypt falls after Antony and Cleopatra's defeat at Actium — the richest kingdom on earth becomes Rome's breadbasket.

27 BC: Octavian takes the name Augustus. The Republic is dead; the Empire begins.

5/ 43 AD: Emperor Claudius invades Britain.

By 84 AD, General Agricola pushes as far as Scotland, winning at Mons Graupius — the farthest north Rome will ever hold ground.

6/ By the early 200s AD, Rome stretches over 2 million square miles across three continents — Hadrian's Wall to the Euphrates.

It took 500 years to build. It would take less than 300 to fall apart.
